transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (SE), Priya (CSM); Lena (Talaria Head of ML), Samir (DevOps), Grace (CTO), Evan (Product)

Summary: quick handoff from sales to delivery; confirm network/VPC details, KMS/encryption, staging runbook, pilot benchmarks and timeline; align on success criteria and next steps.

Topics: onboarding timeline; VPC peering and egress rules; SSO/SCIM and RBAC for console; data retention & audit logs; pilot perf targets and test harness; initial rollout plan and rollback strategy.

Action items (as discussed in-call): see metadata action_items list above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: ok uh good afternoon everyone thanks for making the time, I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. quick roundtable?
[00:18] Grace Monroe: hi Grace here, CTO at Talaria, Samir and Lena are with me.
[00:25] Samir Patel: Samir, DevOps.
[00:27] Lena Ortiz: Lena, head of ML. Hey.
[00:29] Maya Chen: awesome, thanks. Priya and Jonah from our onboarding team will take the technical bits.
[00:34] Priya Natarajan: hi all, Priya, CSM, i'll own the runbook coordination and timeline.
[00:40] Jonah Rivera: Jonah, SE — i'll run the perf checklist and the staging tests.
[00:45] Evan Brooks: Evan, product — here to make sure success metrics map to roadmap.

[01:05] Maya Chen: rough agenda — we'll confirm infra handoff details, review our staging plan, perf/pilot windows, and agree success criteria + next steps. any additions?
[01:15] Grace Monroe: maybe cover compliance items — audit logs, retention, and KMS.
[01:20] Priya Natarajan: yes we'll cover those under security.

[02:02] Jonah Rivera: ok jumping in — from a hosting perspective you told us you want private deployment in your VPC and the redwood private control plane — correct? (note: some transcripts may show 'redwood private' typed as 'Redwood Privatee').
[02:18] Lena Ortiz: yes private, we can't have model data leaving our VPC for PHI reasons.
[02:22] Samir Patel: we need details for peering and firewall, and we use a customer-managed KMS (Hashi HSM), so key wrap integration is required.
[02:32] Jonah Rivera: got it. we support KMS integrations — our Private build supports external KMS and HSM flows. we'll need the KMS contact and the service principals, plus the CIDR ranges.

[03:05] Grace Monroe: what about egress to telemetry/observability? we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[03:12] Priya Natarajan: yes we have a routing option to stream audit logs to customer endpoints — it's configurable. i'll add the log forwarding doc link in notes (link shared later).

[04:00] Evan Brooks: curious about console access — we want SCIM + SSO and fine-grained RBAC, is that on roadmap or GA?
[04:12] Jonah Rivera: SCIM & SSO via SAML is GA on the Private plane, RBAC roles we can seed; some minor RBAC scopes are still in rollout but we can configure perms for your staging users.
[04:32] Lena Ortiz: any gotchas with session length or long-running model evals? we run longer context windows sometimes.
[04:40] Jonah Rivera: session ttl is configurable; bigger concern is KV cache and memory pressure on large context — for those we recommended our ded-quant profile or higher memory instances on Dedicated/pvt. we'll propose config options in the perf plan.

[05:20] Maya Chen: let's align on the pilot — Priya you proposed a 3-day pilot for perf?
[05:28] Priya Natarajan: yes three full days in staging, run our standard perf harness (p50, p95, throughput) plus a subset of your production prompts for quality checks.
[05:36] Grace Monroe: timeline: we'd like to be in pilot by Dec 8 if possible. is that still feasible?
[05:42] Jonah Rivera: should be — assuming network and KMS are in place. we need the VPC info by Dec 4.

[06:25] Samir Patel: to confirm, you'll do a transient peering and then we remove when done? we prefer least privilege.
[06:32] Jonah Rivera: peering is ephemeral for the pilot but for Private it's a long-lived peering; we can do ephemeral tunneling for the test window. i'll note that.

[07:10] Evan Brooks: success criteria, from product side: p95 generation < 350ms for trimmed prompts, token accuracy within our baseline (we'll provide test set) and no more than 0.5% error rate on extraction tasks.
[07:25] Priya Natarajan: we'll capture that in the success criteria doc.

[08:00] Grace Monroe: compliance: SOC2 scope, encryption at rest and in-flight, and audit logs. do you have SOC2 cert copy and details?
[08:10] Maya Chen: yes SOC2 report available — i'll send, and our Private deployment also supports customer-managed key wrapping. for in-flight TLS is always on.
[08:22] Lena Ortiz: we might also request a pen-test scope.
[08:26] Maya Chen: ok we'll coordinate with security for that, i've noted as an action.

[09:05] Jonah Rivera: small note on models — you'll be using a quantized open model; we recommend the 4-bit dynamic quant profile for memory/latency tradeoff. there's slight quality delta we'd validate in the pilot.
[09:20] Lena Ortiz: yes we will run extractive QA on the pilot dataset to confirm.

[10:00] Samir Patel: network specifics — we use a strict egress policy and restrict outbound to only specific endpoints. can the private plane call-home be locked to IP ranges?
[10:10] Jonah Rivera: yes we can lock egress to a set of IPs and ports; we'll provide the list. note: some telemetry endpoints are optional.

[11:00] Evan Brooks: what about rollout plan — how do we version models and do canaries?
[11:08] Priya Natarajan: our console supports model pinning and canary rollouts; SE can help configure a 10% canary with auto-fallback to previous model on quality regression.
[11:22] Jonah Rivera: and we have delta alerts if evals drop vs baseline.

[12:05] Grace Monroe: ok on cost — can you provide guidance on Dedicated vs Private cost delta? we may start private but want committed reserved capacity later.
[12:15] Maya Chen: yes — pricing deck will be shared, a rough rule: Private has infra and support line items; Dedicated reserved capacity gives predictable unit cost at scale. i'll attach an example worksheet for your workload.

[13:00] (crosstalk) Samir Patel: also what about backups of KV cache, do we persist?
[13:05] Jonah Rivera: KV cache is ephemeral by design; we can snapshot context for debugging but we don't persist customer KV long-term unless requested and governed by retention policy.

[14:00] Priya Natarajan: ok i'll recap timeline: 1) Talaria provides VPC CIDR and KMS contact by 2026-12-04; 2) Redwood shares staging runbook + network diagram by 2026-12-02; 3) SE/Customer schedule pilot week of 2026-12-08.

[14:30] Grace Monroe: that works, is there a template for the prompts and evals you want?
[14:36] Jonah Rivera: yes we'll share a prompt set and the perf harness repo link. we'll also accept your prod-like prompts for the quality run.

[15:05] Evan Brooks: slight concern — Anthropic's recent inference pricing is lower but they don't offer our control plane features. any notes we should weigh?
[15:15] Maya Chen: totally — tradeoff is control vs cost; we emphasized predictable SLAs, private deployment, KMS, and tracing/audit for regulated workloads. we'll include a comparison doc.

[16:00] Lena Ortiz: small transcription note — earlier you mentioned KV cache as 'K-V cash' which made us laugh, just flagging the transcript.
[16:08] (laughter)

[17:00] Jonah Rivera: now some specifics for the perf run: target endpoints per second, concurrency level, typical prompt length are needed. Samir or Evan can supply concurrency and average token length.
[17:12] Samir Patel: average token length ~ 600 tokens per request, concurrency we expect 8-12 sustained during peak.

[18:00] Jonah Rivera: ok we'll set up load generator accordingly; we'll also capture p50/p95/p99 with token-level breakdown in the report.

[19:00] Priya Natarajan: security doc link: https://redwood.example.com/security/talaria-scope (Note: we will attach the official SOC2 PDF in follow up).

[20:00] Grace Monroe: about SSO, we already have Okta SCIM, can we onboard via SCIM and map groups?
[20:08] Jonah Rivera: yes, Okta SCIM is supported, we can map Okta groups to RBAC roles. i'll coordinate with your identity engineer.

[22:00] Evan Brooks: rollback — if canary fails, what's the fastest path to fallback?
[22:08] Jonah Rivera: auto-fallback policy triggers immediate routing back to previous model; monitoring shows the fail within a minute and rollback is near instantaneous at the router layer. we'll test this in pilot.

[23:30] Samir Patel: will we get an infra diagram for where the Private control plane sits relative to our VPC?
[23:40] Priya Natarajan: yes diagram will be included in runbook (see earlier link).

[25:00] Maya Chen: ok let's talk admin: who owns runbook approvals on your side?
[25:08] Grace Monroe: i'll own the sign-off with Samir.

[26:30] Priya Natarajan: outstanding items — pen-test scope, SOC2 copy, KMS contact, VPC CIDR; we'll consolidate in a follow-up email with attachments.

[28:00] Evan Brooks: about model updates — if we want a custom fine-tune later how is that handled in Private?
[28:10] Jonah Rivera: fine-tune workflows can be run in Private, but we recommend storing artifacts in your object store; we support registering model artifacts into the catalog with versioning. we'll walk through that in a separate session.

[30:00] (brief pause)
[30:20] Maya Chen: any blockers we haven't touched?
[30:25] Lena Ortiz: just internal scheduling, otherwise no blockers.

[32:00] Samir Patel: one more network nuance — we use strict MTLS for service-to-service in prod, can Redwood present client certs?
[32:10] Jonah Rivera: we can support mTLS for some endpoints; i'll confirm which endpoints allow client cert auth and which rely on IP whitelisting.

[34:00] Priya Natarajan: ok because of that i'll add a checklist item for cert exchange.

[36:00] Evan Brooks: question on observability retention windows — can we keep traces and token-level logs for 90 days?
[36:10] Jonah Rivera: default is 30 days, extended retention is an add-on. we can propose retention SLAs in the enterprise package.

[38:00] Grace Monroe: fine, we'll note that as a potential add-on.

[40:00] Maya Chen: recap and commitments: Redwood will send runbook + network diagram by 2026-12-02, SE perf plan by 2026-12-03, Talaria to provide VPC/KMS by 2026-12-04. pilot target week of 2026-12-08.

[41:45] Priya Natarajan: i'll put calendar invites for the pilot prep and the 3-day run.

[42:10] Evan Brooks: please include any required firewall rules and a sample iptables snippet.

[43:00] (crosstalk)

[44:30] Maya Chen: items for our sales/legal team — Grace requested SOC2 + pen-test scope. I'll attach those in the follow-up.

[46:00] Samir Patel: small ask — during the pilot can you mute non-essential telemetry to minimize data leaving the VPC?
[46:08] Jonah Rivera: yes telemetry toggles exist; critical telemetry for debugging we keep, optional we can turn off.

[47:30] Lena Ortiz: also, we'll send a 200-record prompt sample for quality checks.

[49:00] Priya Natarajan: thanks all, i'll circulate notes and action items within 24 hours.

[50:00] Grace Monroe: thanks team — sounds like we have a clear path.
[50:06] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the runbook and links.
[51:00] (meeting ends)

Shared artifacts referenced: onboarding runbook (link), perf harness repo (link), SOC2 PDF (attached later), pricing worksheet (shared after call).
